# Results — Study 672 (McGinley Dynamic)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
John McGinley's "Dynamic" line **auto-adjusts its own speed to price**, "hugs" it more
tightly than a fixed SMA/EMA of the same nominal length, and so gives **cleaner
crossovers (fewer whipsaws)** — turned into an honest race: a McGinley Dynamic(14)
price-cross long/flat rule vs the same rule on SMA(14) and EMA(14), vs buy-and-hold, net
of one-way costs × NAV, on a five-ticker liquid basket (SPY, QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, XLE, daily
total-return bars). Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | Rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| SPY  | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30 | 8,411  | `a17d226a750c` |
| QQQ  | 1999-03-10 → 2026-06-30 | 6,869  | `d4803f2cacfd` |
| AAPL | 1980-12-12 → 2026-06-30 | 11,478 | `e74358d3eb78` |
| MSFT | 1986-03-13 → 2026-06-30 | 10,152 | `b40f0005f6bd` |
| XLE  | 1998-12-22 → 2026-06-30 | 6,921  | `e427f1851a43` |

Bars are Yahoo daily, **total-return** (`auto_adjust=True` folds splits/dividends into
the close). No survivorship on the Signal axis — these are five large, currently-liquid
tapes (not a "top-N momentum" survivor panel), and the claim under test is about the
*indicator's mechanism*, not a cross-sectional selection.

## The mechanism — does McGinley Dynamic actually "hug price" / react faster?

The whole pitch rests on the `^4` term in `MD(t) = MD(t-1) + (P(t)-MD(t-1)) / (N *
(P(t)/MD(t-1))^4)` making the line speed up when price runs and slow down in chop. Two
direct, deterministic checks:

| Check | McGinley Dynamic(14) | SMA(14) | EMA(14) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Mean `\|close − line\| / close` (SPY, real tape) | **1.981%** | 1.535% | **1.327%** |
| +20% step response: gap closed 5 bars after the shock | **20.2%** | 42.9% | **57.6%** |

Both point the same way, and it is the **opposite** of the marketing pitch: on the real
SPY tape the McGinley line sits *farther* from price on average than either a plain SMA
or EMA of the same length, and on a clean deterministic step it reacts *slower* — the
quartic denominator brakes the update exactly when price is moving fastest (the moment a
trader most wants the line to keep up). "Auto-adjusting" is a real mechanism; it is not
the mechanism advertised.

## The headline — SPY, net of 5 bps one-way cost

| Rule | Sharpe (net) | CAGR (net) | Max DD | active spread (bps/day) | HAC *t* | switches/yr | time in mkt |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **McGinley Dynamic(14)** | **0.380** | **3.81%** | −49.1% | **−3.01** | **−3.55** | **25.5** | 70% |
| SMA(14) cross | 0.238 | 2.07% | −57.6% | −3.70 | −4.42 | 36.5 | 63% |
| EMA(14) cross | 0.267 | 2.40% | −48.0% | −3.57 | −4.22 | 38.3 | 65% |
| **Buy & hold** | **0.647** | **10.83%** | −55.2% | — | — | 0 | 100% |

- All three moving-average timing rules **lose to buy-and-hold**, McGinley Dynamic
  included: **−3.01 bps/day at HAC *t* = −3.55**, significant and on the wrong side.
  Sitting out 30% of a bull tape is the cost; the timing does not pay for it.
- The **gross** (cost = 0) spread is **−2.51 bps/day, HAC *t* = −2.98** — costs widen
  the hole but are not the root cause; the timing itself is negative.

## "Fewer whipsaws than a plain MA?" — the headline claim, measured literally

| Rule | switches/yr (SPY) | vs SMA | vs EMA |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **McGinley Dynamic(14)** | **25.5** | **−30%** | **−33%** |
| SMA(14) | 36.5 | — | — |
| EMA(14) | 38.3 | — | — |

Unlike the desk's other "smarter moving average" teardowns — the Hull MA (Study 432,
+87% *more* switches than SMA) and Kaufman's KAMA (Study 433, +66% *more* turnover) —
**McGinley Dynamic genuinely fires fewer position changes**: 25.5/yr vs the SMA's 36.5
and the EMA's 38.3, a real 30-33% cut, and the pattern holds basket-wide (see per-instrument
table below). The literal "fewer false signals" claim is **not busted on this metric** —
it is the one part of the folklore that survives contact with the tape.

## "Cleaner / better than the plain MA it claims to beat?" — head-to-head

Fewer trades only matters if they are *better* trades. HAC *t* of the McGinley-minus-SMA
and McGinley-minus-EMA daily net-return spread (SPY, cost = 5 bps):

| Comparison | spread (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| McGinley Dynamic − SMA(14) | +0.69 | +1.43 |
| McGinley Dynamic − EMA(14) | +0.56 | +1.46 |

Positive on paper, on SPY — but **neither clears *t* = 2**. Per-instrument (below), only
3 of 10 such head-to-head comparisons across the five-ticker basket do.

## Permutation placebo — is the timing real, or just exposure?

Hold the realised McGinley Dynamic position path's block structure but circularly shift
it against returns (destroys the timing, keeps turnover and net-long bias), 2,000 draws,
gross spread statistic:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Observed McGinley Dynamic spread | −2.51 bps/day |
| Placebo mean spread | −1.43 bps/day |
| One-sided *p* (placebo ≥ observed) | **0.9895** |

Almost every one of the 2,000 random re-timings beats the real McGinley calls — the
timing carries **negative** information on this tape, the same failure mode as the
desk's other adaptive-MA teardowns (432, 433).

## Cost sweep (SPY, McGinley Dynamic(14))

| round-trip cost | net Sharpe | active spread (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | 0.489 | −2.51 | −2.98 |
| 2.0 bps | 0.445 | −2.71 | −3.21 |
| 5.0 bps | 0.380 | −3.01 | −3.55 |
| 10.0 bps | 0.270 | −3.52 | −4.10 |

The spread is negative before any cost is charged — there is no break-even cost that
rescues it.

## Per-instrument (McGinley Dynamic(14) long/flat, cost = 5 bps)

| Ticker | MD Sharpe (net) | Buy&hold Sharpe | active spread (bps/day) | HAC *t* | MD−SMA *t* | MD−EMA *t* | switches/yr MD / SMA / EMA |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 0.380 | 0.647 | −3.01 | −3.55 | +1.43 | +1.46 | 25.5 / 36.5 / 38.3 |
| QQQ  | 0.470 | 0.521 | −2.29 | −1.81 | **+2.38** | **+2.75** | 26.0 / 36.6 / 39.8 |
| AAPL | 0.632 | 0.623 | −2.69 | −1.70 | +0.13 | −0.30 | 23.5 / 33.1 / 35.7 |
| MSFT | 0.494 | 0.821 | −5.89 | −5.35 | +0.75 | +0.69 | 26.7 / 37.3 / 40.9 |
| XLE  | 0.269 | 0.428 | −2.78 | −1.89 | +1.26 | **+2.09** | 29.6 / 36.6 / 42.4 |

**Five of five** instruments: the McGinley timing underperforms buy-and-hold (negative
spread, two of five individually significant at |*t*| ≥ 2 — SPY, MSFT). Against the
plain MAs it claims to beat, only QQQ (both comparisons) and XLE (vs EMA) clear *t* = 2 —
positive on paper everywhere, certified almost nowhere.

## Robustness — in/out-of-sample split (SPY, McGinley Dynamic(14), cost = 5 bps)

| Half | MD Sharpe (net) | Buy&hold Sharpe | active spread (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| First half (1993–2009) | 0.234 | 0.455 | −2.45 | −1.89 |
| Second half (2009–2026) | 0.572 | 0.872 | −3.47 | −3.09 |

Negative in **both** halves; the underperformance is not a single-regime artefact.

## Long/short variant (SPY, cost = 5 bps, borrow 50 bps/yr)

Flipping to short when McGinley Dynamic is falling makes it worse: net Sharpe **−0.178**,
active spread **−6.08 bps/day** at HAC *t* = **−3.58**. Shorting an upward-drifting index
on a lagging trend signal compounds the loss.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic regime-switching-trend tape (`data.synthetic_panel`, planted-edge knob);
no network.

| World | McGinley active spread (bps/day) | HAC *t* | net Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.39** (sd 1.12), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** | | |
| planted edge = 0.3 (seed 672) | +12.27 | **+9.86** | +2.33 |
| planted edge = 0.6 (seed 672) | +26.27 | **+15.23** | +4.72 |
| planted edge = 1.0 (seed 672) | +13.06 | **+8.27** | +1.66 |

The null fires on essentially none of 20 independent streams (1/20 ≈ the ~5% false-positive
rate expected at a *t* = 2 threshold — not systematic bias), and a planted trend lights up
hard. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** McGinley Dynamic(14) timing's active spread vs buy-and-hold is
  **−3.01 bps/day at HAC *t* = −3.55** on SPY (gross *t* = −2.98), negative on all five
  basket tapes, in both sample halves, and the long/short variant is worse still
  (*t* = −3.58). The permutation placebo gives *p* = 0.9895 — the timing is *worse* than
  random. The "auto-adjusting" line does not add positive timing information on daily
  US equities.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net Sharpe 0.380 vs buy-and-hold's 0.647 (gross 0.489, still
  behind); no cost level rescues it, there is no break-even, and the long/short version
  is outright destructive.
- **Cuts whipsaws & beats a plain MA? — MIXED.** The one part of the folklore that
  survives: McGinley Dynamic really does fire **30-33% fewer** position changes than
  SMA(14)/EMA(14) of the same length (25.5 vs 36.5/38.3 switches/yr, basket-wide). But
  the stated *mechanism* is backwards — it tracks price *more loosely* (1.98% vs EMA's
  1.33%) and reacts *slower* to a shock (closes 20% of a step gap in 5 bars vs EMA's
  58%) — and the fewer, slower trades only clear *t* ≥ 2 against SMA/EMA on 3 of 10
  basket comparisons. Fewer signals, yes; *smarter* signals, not shown.
